import numpy as np

# 1. READ DATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

ADJ_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

adj = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)

# 2. COMPUTE THE CHANGE 2021→2022 AND DROP BOROUGHS WITH MISSING Δ
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
df["delta"] = df["NO2_2022"] - df["NO2_2021"]
df_nonmiss = df.dropna(subset=["delta"]).copy()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. BUILD UNDIRECTED ADJACENCY DICTIONARY
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Start with every borough present in either col as key (even if isolated for now)
adj_dict = {}
for b, n in zip(adj["borough"], adj["neighbor"]):
    adj_dict.setdefault(b, set()).add(n)
    adj_dict.setdefault(n, set()).add(b)        # make it undirected

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. KEEP ONLY BOROUGHS WITH DATA  &  REMOVE ISOLATES (no neighbours left)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
available = set(df_nonmiss["borough"])
# Iteratively drop isolates that lose all neighbours once we limit to "available"
changed = True
while changed:
    changed = False
    isolates = {b for b in available if len(adj_dict.get(b, set()) & available) == 0}
    if isolates:
        available -= isolates
        changed = True

# Final filtered DataFrame
df_final = df_nonmiss[df_nonmiss["borough"].isin(available)].set_index("borough")
N = len(df_final)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. BUILD ROW-STANDARDISED WEIGHT MATRIX  (sparse, dict-of-dicts)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
weights = {}
for b in df_final.index:
    nbrs = list(adj_dict[b] & available)
    w = 1.0 / len(nbrs)            # row-standardised (all rows sum to 1)
    weights[b] = {n: w for n in nbrs}

# S0 (sum of all weights) after standardisation is simply N
S0 = float(N)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. GLOBAL MORAN’S I
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
x = df_final["delta"].to_numpy()
x_mean = x.mean()
z = x - x_mean
den = np.sum(z**2)

num = 0.0
for i, bi in enumerate(df_final.index):
    zi = z[i]
    for bj, wij in weights[bi].items():
        zj = z[df_final.index.get_loc(bj)]
        num += wij * zi * zj

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. PERMUTATION TEST (two-sided)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
n_perm = 1000
I_perm = np.empty(n_perm)

for k in range(n_perm):
    shuffle = rng.permutation(x)
    z_perm = shuffle - shuffle.mean()
    den_p = np.sum(z_perm**2)
    num_p = 0.0
    for i, bi in enumerate(df_final.index):
        zi_p = z_perm[i]
        for bj, wij in weights[bi].items():
            zj_p = z_perm[df_final.index.get_loc(bj)]
            num_p += wij * zi_p * zj_p
    I_perm[k] = (N / S0) * (num_p / den_p)

# two-sided p-value
p_val = np.mean(np.abs(I_perm) >= abs(I_obs))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. VERDICT
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
if (p_val < 0.05) and (I_obs > 0):
    verdict = "CLUSTERED"
else:
    verdict = "NOT CLUSTERED"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. REQUIRED PRINT STATEMENTS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"data_points_used = {N}")

import numpy as np

NO2_PATH = "chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_2021_2022_no2.csv"
ADJACENCY_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(NO2_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# -------------------------------
# 2. Compute the change 2021 ➜ 2022
# -------------------------------
df["dNO2"] = df["NO2_2022"] - df["NO2_2021"]

# -------------------------------
# 3. Exclude boroughs with missing change
# -------------------------------
df_valid = df.dropna(subset=["dNO2"]).reset_index(drop=True)

# -------------------------------
# 4. Build a symmetric neighbour list
# -------------------------------
# Make sure the neighbour info is symmetric
sym_adj = pd.concat(
    [
        adj,
        adj.rename(columns={"borough": "neighbor", "neighbor": "borough"}),
    ],
    ignore_index=True,
)

# Keep only boroughs that survived the missing-value filter
valid_set = set(df_valid["borough"])
sym_adj = sym_adj[sym_adj["borough"].isin(valid_set) & sym_adj["neighbor"].isin(valid_set)]

# -------------------------------
# 5. Build the (row-standardised) weight matrix W
# -------------------------------
boroughs = sorted(valid_set)  # list of boroughs in a fixed order
index = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}
N = len(boroughs)

# Start with a zero matrix
W = np.zeros((N, N), dtype=float)

for _, row in sym_adj.iterrows():
    i = index[row["borough"]]
    j = index[row["neighbor"]]
    if i != j:
        W[i, j] = 1.0

# Row-standardise: divide each row by its sum
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
# Identify rows with at least one neighbour
non_isolated = row_sums > 0

# If any borough became isolated after neighbour filtering, drop it
if not np.all(non_isolated):

    W = W[keep_indices][:, keep_indices]
    boroughs = [boroughs[i] for i in keep_indices]
    df_valid = df_valid.set_index("borough").loc[boroughs].reset_index()
    N = len(boroughs)
    row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)

W = W / row_sums[:, None]  # row-standardised
S0 = W.sum()               # should equal N after standardisation

# -------------------------------

# -------------------------------
